title: JavaScript Iterators and Generators
description: Model iterable and iterator protocols, trace lazy generator execution, and use early termination and cleanup safely.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish an iterable, an iterator, and a generator object.
Trace next(), yield, and the done/value result without confusing a generator's return value with a yielded item.
Choose lazy iteration when it helps, and avoid eager materialization of large or unbounded sequences.
Use early exit and finally cleanup safely, and explain how async generators differ.

blocks.text: Three related ideas: iterable, iterator, generator

An iterable describes how to obtain an iterator, usually through [Symbol.iterator](). An iterator has next(), which returns an object with done and optionally value. A generator function written function* creates a generator object: calling it does not run its body yet; each next() resumes execution until the next yield or completion. This protocol is what lets for...of consume arrays, strings, Maps, and generators through one interface.

blocks.title: Do not confuse the collection with its cursor
blocks.text: A reusable iterable can create a fresh iterator for each traversal. A generator object is itself an iterator and is normally one-shot: after it is exhausted, another loop over the same generator object has no values. Call the generator function again to get a fresh one.

steps.title: Calling the generator creates a paused iterator
steps.explanation: The function body has not run just because range(2, 4) was called. The generator object retains the local execution state and resumes only when next() is requested.

steps.title: Each yield pauses and provides one value
steps.explanation: The first next() enters the body and runs to yield 2. The following next() resumes after that yield, increments current, and yields 3.

steps.title: Completion reports done and the return value
steps.explanation: After the last yielded value, the next call finishes the loop and returns 4 with done: true. That completion value is not another yielded item and is not included by for...of.

blocks.prompt: What happens immediately when `const sequence = makeSequence()` calls a generator function?

options.text: The generator body runs to completion and stores every value in an array
options.feedback: A generator call creates a paused generator object; values are produced as it is advanced.

options.text: A generator object is returned, and its body begins when next() advances it
options.feedback: Generator execution is suspended at creation and resumes on next(), running until yield or completion.

options.text: The function becomes asynchronous and returns a Promise
options.feedback: A synchronous generator returns a generator object, not a Promise. An async generator uses async function*.

options.text: The function can no longer be called again
options.feedback: Each call creates a new generator object with its own execution state.

blocks.explanation: The call creates the iterator; iteration demand controls when the body advances.

steps.title: Expose a fresh iterator from the iterable
steps.explanation: The object implements [Symbol.iterator] as a generator method. Each call creates a new generator, so alphabet can be traversed repeatedly.

steps.title: Spread asks the iterator for every value
steps.explanation: Spread consumes the iterator until done and eagerly stores the values in a new array. This is convenient for small finite data but can use substantial memory.

steps.title: A saved iterator represents one traversal
steps.explanation: oneShot is the iterator itself, not a reusable collection. Once exhausted, consuming it again yields nothing; a new iterator must be requested.

blocks.title: Lazy production does not make eager consumers lazy
blocks.text: A generator can produce a very large or unbounded sequence without first allocating every item. But [...generator] and Array.from(generator) consume it all into memory; they never finish for an infinite sequence. Prefer for...of with an explicit stop condition or bounded iteration when the source may be large.

blocks.prompt: A generator yields 1 and 2, then executes `return 99`. What does `for (const value of generator) console.log(value)` print?

options.feedback: for...of stops when done becomes true and does not expose the iterator's completion return value as an item.
Only yielded values are visited. The final return value is available through a manual next() result where done is true.
return completes the generator after the preceding yield values; it does not replace them.

options.text: Nothing, because return is invalid in a generator
options.feedback: A generator may return a completion value; iteration syntax simply does not treat it as another yielded value.

blocks.explanation: Distinguish yield values consumed by the iteration protocol from the final completion value returned by next().

steps.title: Place resource cleanup in finally
steps.explanation: A generator that owns a resource or subscription can use try/finally so normal completion and iterator closure share cleanup logic.

steps.title: Understand break behavior
steps.explanation: Breaking from for...of closes the iterator by calling its return() method when available. That resumes the generator's completion path and runs finally before the loop exits.

blocks.text: A synchronous generator yields ordinary values; yielding a Promise does not make it an async generator. An async generator is declared with async function* and returns an async iterator whose next() produces Promises. Consume it with for await...of in an async context. Use async iteration for streamed or incremental asynchronous data, not as a default replacement for a normal array or Promise.

blocks.title: Build a bounded lazy page iterator
blocks.context: A report can contain many pages, but a screen may need only the first few until the user requests more. Design iteration so the caller can stop without loading all page numbers into an array.
instructions: Write a generator that yields page numbers from a starting page up to, but not including, an ending page.
Manually call next() for a small range and record value/done for each result, including the final completion.
Consume a fresh generator with for...of and stop after a configured page limit.
Add a try/finally trace and verify that early break closes the iterator.
Explain why spreading the entire sequence is a poor choice for a potentially huge range.
requirements: Boundary behavior is explicit for empty ranges and the end-exclusive limit.
Manual next() results distinguish yielded values from the final return value.
Each traversal uses a fresh iterator.
Early termination runs cleanup exactly as documented.
The solution does not eagerly materialize an unbounded or unnecessarily large sequence.
hints: A generator pauses at yield and resumes after the previous yield on the next call.
for...of consumes only yielded values; a done: true value is not looped over.
Use a new generator call for each independent traversal.
A break closes the iterator; put cleanup in try/finally if the generator owns resources.
successCriteria: Yields the expected half-open range and handles an empty range.
Documents the exact sequence of next() value/done results.
Stops at the caller's limit without creating a full array.
Shows cleanup running when the loop exits early.

items: An iterable provides [Symbol.iterator](); an iterator provides next(); a generator function creates a lazy generator iterator.
yield produces iteration values; return completes iteration and its value is not a for...of item.
Generator objects are one-shot; call the generator function again for a new traversal.
Lazy production can save intermediate allocation, but spread/Array.from eagerly consume the sequence.
Early iterator closure can run generator finally cleanup; async generators use for await...of.
